extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom style guide for inclusive, accurate and sensitive language when reporting about race, ethnicity, disability, gender, religion and other identity-related topics. It provides preferred terms, discouraged terms and usage notes for journalists and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: American Indian / Native American — tribal membership and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal membership is determined by tribes; federal government considers someone American Indian if they belong to a federally recognized tribe. Individual tribes have exclusive right to determine membership and may require specific lineage thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume ancestry confers tribal membership; use native-born to describe someone born in the U.S. who isn't American Indian. Note: 2016 legislation (HR 4238) replaced the term American Indian with Native American in federal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: native-born
rubrics_metrics.description: Use native-born to describe someone who is born in the United States but isn't American Indian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Hawaiian — identity and origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Native Hawaiians (Kanaka Maoli) trace lineage and language to Polynesians including Tahitians, Maoris and Samoans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting in 2000 the federal government recognized Native Hawaiians and Pacific Islanders as a distinct group, including in Census counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander — U.S. Census definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Census Bureau defines 'Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander' as a person having origins in any of the original peoples of Hawaii, Guam, Samoa, or other Pacific Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The racial categories reflect social definitions and sociocultural groups rather than biological or anthropological definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander (umbrella term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Umbrella term used by U.S. Census and other agencies for people who trace roots to original peoples of Hawaii, Guam, Samoa or other Pacific Islands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negro (avoid as descriptor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use 'Negro' to describe a person of African descent; use African American or black instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term is acceptable in organization names and historical references (e.g., National Council of Negro Women) and in historical context. Do not use 'Negress'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negro Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: See Black codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negro National Anthem (historical usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to the poem/song 'Lift Ev’ry Voice and Sing' (1899) adopted by the NAACP and representing resilience and strength of Black people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in historical context and provide context about significance; example excerpt and recording note included.

rubrics_metrics.name: neo-paganism
rubrics_metrics.description: Term describing contemporary paganism as opposed to ancient paganism; some prefer 'pagan' or 'neo-pagan' depending on emphasis on blending old and new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nepali / Nepalese usage
rubrics_metrics.description: People from Nepal may be called Nepalese or Nepali; 'Nepali' is favored in current usage and can be noun or adjective. U.S. press sometimes uses Nepalese for those in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use context-appropriate form; e.g., Nepali sari, Nepali government official.

rubrics_metrics.name: neuroatypical / neurodivergent — usage and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms for people with atypical developmental, intellectual and cognitive abilities (e.g., autism and other developmental differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These terms are used by some in the autism community to avoid ableist language and to acknowledge differences and strengths. An individual may be neurodivergent; a group can be neurodiverse. Medical community acceptance varies; include signs listed by NINDS when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: neurodiversity — concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Neurodiversity is the concept that neurological differences like autism are normal variations in the human brain and that such differences can confer strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses origins, scope (may include dyslexia, Tourette Syndrome, etc.), and the Neurodiversity Movement's social-justice aims for inclusion and equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: neurotypical / neurologically typical
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used to describe people with typical developmental, intellectual and cognitive abilities; often described in relation to those with autism or other differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These terms are increasingly used outside medicine; list common traits (no speech delays, ability to adapt, etc.). See neuroatypical, neurodivergent.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Age movement
rubrics_metrics.description: A loose spiritual movement from the late 1960s combining religion, psychology and parapsychology and influenced by native practices and mysticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Followers construct individualized spiritual journeys; mention when relevant and avoid over-generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: niggardly — caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Word means stingy or miserly but can be perceived as insulting because it sounds like the slur 'nigger.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with usage due to potential perception issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: nigger (racial slur) — usage restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A highly offensive racial slur for Black people; also known as the n-word. Avoid use except in extremely compelling situations with supervisor approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use unless necessary for reporting/quoting; treat with caution and context. Notes on intra-community uses and variants like 'nigga' acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: niqab — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A veil worn by some Muslim women covering all of the face except the eyes.

rubrics_metrics.name: nirvana — meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Means bliss or state of freedom from the cycle of reincarnations in Buddhism; from Sanskrit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nisei / generational terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Nisei refers to U.S.-born children of Japanese immigrants (second generation) and implies being raised in the U.S.; related terms include Issei (first generation), Sansei (third), Yonsei (fourth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization conventions vary by institution; some capitalize when used in a generational context or as part of proper nouns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nollywood — definition and origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Nigeria's film industry, named by analogy to Hollywood/Bollywood; third largest producer of feature films though many are low-budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include origin anecdote and contextual economic/production details when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: non-binary gender — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender identities that don't fit within the male/female binary; people can feel both, neither or a mixture.

rubrics_metrics.name: non-binary pronouns — avoid the phrase 'non-binary pronouns'
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid saying 'non-binary pronouns' because not all non-binary people use the same pronouns and other genders also use they/them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead use: gender-neutral pronouns, they/them pronouns, or pronouns. See gender-neutral pronouns.

rubrics_metrics.name: non-disabled — term guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-disabled is used to refer to someone who does not have a disability and is acceptable; avoid 'able-bodied' in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: nonbinary / non-binary — definition and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Umbrella term for people whose gender identity/expression falls outside man/woman binary; may or may not identify as transgender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult sources when possible; note alternative cultural terms (Two-Spirit, Third Gender) and encourage asking subjects about pronouns.

rubrics_metrics.name: noncitizen / undocumented noncitizen — preferred government language
rubrics_metrics.description: Noncitizen describes someone not a citizen; undocumented noncitizen describes someone living without official permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. government agencies have moved away from 'illegal alien' and 'alien' in favor of these terms (USCIS memo, Feb 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: nuts (see crazy)
rubrics_metrics.description: See 'crazy' (implicit cross-reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: obese / obesity — people-first language
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer people-first language when writing about people with obesity: say 'person with obesity' or 'people with obesity' rather than 'obese person'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid judgmental phrases (weight problem, fat); recognize some in Fat Acceptance Movement embrace 'fat' but it may be offensive to many and should be used only when subjects prefer it. Use neutral terms like weight or excess weight. Consult Rethink Obesity, Guidelines for Media Portrayals, and World Obesity Federation resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: obituaries (LGBT) — survivors listing
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting survivors, list partners of gay, lesbian, bisexual or transgender deceased in an order equivalent to spouses of heterosexual deceased.

rubrics_metrics.name: obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) — diagnosis and reference
rubrics_metrics.description: OCD is an anxiety disorder with unreasonable thoughts and repetitive behaviors; refer to someone as having OCD only if relevant and formally diagnosed by a reputable source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'obsessive-compulsive disorder' on first reference; 'OCD' is acceptable on second reference. Do not use OCD as a casual adjective for undiagnosed behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Okies — pejorative
rubrics_metrics.description: Pejorative term for people from Oklahoma dating from the Dust Bowl/Great Depression; avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: older (people, adults, individuals, Americans) — preferred generic term
rubrics_metrics.description: A national survey of age-beat journalists found 'older' to be the top choice as a neutral, flexible descriptor for people in later life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'older' when appropriate as a neutral descriptor.

rubrics_metrics.name: om (Hinduism) — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: In Hinduism, 'om' is the mantra of the divine and the ancient Sanskrit name for the absolute; mantras often begin with om.

rubrics_metrics.name: openly gay/openly lesbian — usage as modifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'openly' when relevant, often in historical context to indicate someone publicly identified as gay/lesbian (e.g., 'the first openly gay...'). Mention sexual orientation only when relevant and avoid terms like acknowledged/admitted/confessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updated Feb 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: opposite sex — consider 'different sex'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'opposite sex' can be offensive or inaccurate for people who don't identify within a binary gender; consider 'different sex' instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alternative phrasing when appropriate for inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oreo — derogatory slang
rubrics_metrics.description: Derogatory term for someone perceived to have shunned black culture; do not use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Uncle Tom' for related pejoratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oriental — use for things not people
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use 'Oriental' to describe people; it is widely considered offensive. It can be used for items like 'Oriental rugs' or 'Oriental medicine.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2016 legislation (HR 4238) replaced 'Oriental' with 'Asian American' in federal laws. Updated Feb 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthodox Church / Orthodox Judaism — capitalization and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Orthodox Church refers to Eastern Christian churches not loyal to the pope; capitalize 'Orthodox' when referring to Judaism and Eastern branches of Christianity or as part of denominational names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orthodox Judaism is the most conservative branch and should be capitalized in all references; Hasidism is a movement within Orthodoxy.

rubrics_metrics.name: orthodox / orthodoxy — lowercase rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Use lowercase 'orthodox'/ 'orthodoxy' when denoting a clear doctrine implying correct belief, except in specific religious proper nouns.

rubrics_metrics.name: out — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who self-identifies as lesbian, gay, bisexual and/or transgender in their personal, public, and/or professional lives; preferred to 'openly gay' as a noun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Ricky Martin is an out pop star.'

rubrics_metrics.name: outing — avoid revealing without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Act of publicly declaring or revealing another person's sexual orientation or gender identity without consent; considered inappropriate by much of the LGBT community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat outing as ethically fraught; avoid unless there is a compelling public-interest reason. See 'coming out', 'closeted.'

rubrics_metrics.name: pagan — definition and capitalization note
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally denotes a person who does not acknowledge Abrahamic God and may worship polytheistic or nature-based religions; modern pagans may prefer capitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note some pagans capitalize the term; be guided by source preference where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paki — absolute prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: A derogatory slur for people of Pakistani origin; do not use under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If quoting, treat with the same caution as other slurs (provide context, indicate offensive nature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pakistani languages — usage note
rubrics_metrics.description: Urdu and English are Pakistan's official languages; other major languages include Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashtu and Balochi; Bengali was formerly official in East Pakistan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate language references when reporting on linguistic topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palestine — historical and modern context
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically a country east of the Mediterranean; today refers to territories under the Palestine National Authority (West Bank, Gaza) and has a distinct national identity moving toward independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain historical shifts (Ottoman, British control, 1948 formation of Israel) and current political status (UN observer state 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Palm Sunday — definition and preferred term
rubrics_metrics.description: The sixth Sunday in Lent beginning Holy Week, marking Jesus' entry into Jerusalem; also known as Passion Sunday though 'Palm Sunday' is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pan-Africanism — definition and symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: A political ideology stressing shared origins and interests of people of African descent and aiming to unify people worldwide; historic roots include DuBois and Marcus Garvey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note symbolism (Pan-African flag colors and meanings) and movement goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: pangender — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A fluid gender identity that might be expressed as both male and female or shift between genders; falls under genderqueer umbrella.

rubrics_metrics.name: pansexual / omnisexual — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone whose primary attraction is to a person regardless of their gender; distinct from heterosexual/homosexual labels that imply gender of partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: paraplegia / paraplegic — people-first language
rubrics_metrics.description: Paraplegia is loss of movement in lower extremities/torso; calling someone 'a paraplegic' can be offensive because it defines them by condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'a person has paraplegia' or note that some people use 'para' in quotes if self-identifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: parent — usage for LGBT parents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'parent' along with mother/father as the proper term for gay, lesbian, bisexual or transgender people raising children; ask subjects which term they prefer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention sexual orientation, genetic relationship or conception technique only when germane. See 'families.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsi / Parsis — pronunciation and identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic group in India that follows Zoroastrianism; pronounced 'PAHR-see.'

rubrics_metrics.name: partition (1947) — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to division of British India into India and Pakistan in 1947, causing massive forced migrations and violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context about regions affected (Punjab, Bengal) and consequences when reporting historical events.

rubrics_metrics.name: partner — neutral relationship term
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly accepted term for people in a committed relationship, including gay/lesbian relationships and unmarried heterosexuals; useful for gender-nonconforming relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See husband, lover, relationships; ask source for preferred term when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pashtun — definition and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethnic group (~18 million) living primarily along Durand Line in Afghanistan and Pakistan; historically rulers of Afghanistan and politically significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate geopolitical context when reporting on Pashtun groups, including Taliban history.

rubrics_metrics.name: passing — definition and historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: When someone appears to be and identifies as a member of another race (e.g., African Americans passing as white to avoid injustice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with historical context and sensitivity; reference relevant literature (e.g., 'Black Like Me').

rubrics_metrics.name: Passover / Pesach — definition and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Jewish holiday commemorating Israelites' freedom from slavery in Egypt; traditional name Pesach and customs (seder, dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Passover' or 'Pesach' appropriately and explain customs for general audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patel motel — stereotype caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Stereotype that people named Patel run many hotels; note statistical data (Asian American Hotels Owners Association) but avoid caricature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on or reinforcing stereotypes in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pearl Harbor — metaphor caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Pearl Harbor' sparingly as a metaphor or analogy because it may invite stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of historical weight and potential insensitivity when using as analogy.

rubrics_metrics.name: people of color — usage and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally acceptable umbrella term for people of races other than White, but it lumps distinct groups together and can evoke strong feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible identify people by their specific racial/ethnic group; avoid acronym 'POC'. See suggested readings on debates about the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: people-first language — definition and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Language that avoids defining a person by a disability (e.g., 'person with a disability' instead of 'the disabled').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use people-first language whenever possible but allow deviations when people-first phrasing is awkward; follow guidance from CDC and relevant professional organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFLAG — naming and inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly 'Parents, Families and Friends of Lesbians and Gays', the organization changed to 'PFLAG' in 2014 for inclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note PFLAG's mission and scope (support, education, advocacy); use updated name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philippine names — conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically follow Western name order; Spanish names are common and nicknames are frequent; Muslim Filipinos may follow special naming rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to naming conventions and cultural specifics when reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilipino / Filipino / Pinoy variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Also Filipino, Pinoy/Pinay; Tagalog terms and gendered variants exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accepted forms and respect subjects' preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: pink triangle — historical and reclamation note
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally a badge gay men were forced to wear in Nazi camps; now reclaimed as a gay pride symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical context when using the symbol in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polock / Polack — derogatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Derogatory slur for Poles; derived from the neutral 'Polak'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use; if quoting, indicate offensive nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: polyamorous vs pansexual — distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Polyamorous means engaging in more than one consensual intimate relationship; pansexual is an orientation attracted regardless of gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse the two; be precise in reporting and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: polygamy — definition and religious context
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice of having more than one spouse; historically practiced by some Mormons (officially ended for mainstream LDS) and permitted in some interpretations of Islam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical/religious context and note contemporary legal and organizational stances.

rubrics_metrics.name: post-racial — contested term
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes a society without racial preference or discrimination; term is controversial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cautiously and provide context and critiques when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) — diagnosis and reference
rubrics_metrics.description: An anxiety disorder that can develop after traumatic events; symptoms and timing described (diagnosis may be a month or more after event).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to someone as having PTSD only if relevant and formally diagnosed by a reputable source. Use full name on first reference and 'PTSD' thereafter; 'flashback' is acceptable to denote reliving events.

rubrics_metrics.name: poverty line / poverty threshold — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Level of income deemed adequate to live in a place; U.S. Federal Poverty Level is calculated annually by HHS and used for program eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain measurement basis (minimum nutrition plus modest non-food allowance) when reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: poverty violations — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Fines and fees for petty violations (fare-hopping, minor offenses, zoning, etc.) that disproportionately affect the poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term when discussing policies that criminalize minor acts and impose financial burdens on low-income people.

rubrics_metrics.name: powwow — restricted usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'powwow' only when referring to the title of a specific American Indian event; avoid using it for general gatherings because it evokes stereotypical images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain origins (Narragansett word for shaman) and cultural meaning (dancing, drumming, honoring traditions) when covering such events.

rubrics_metrics.name: practicing (LGBTQ+) — avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid describing someone's sexual orientation or gender identity as 'practicing' (e.g., 'practicing gay').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'sexually active' when referring to sexual behavior where relevant; do not conflate orientation with behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: pre-lingually deaf / postlingually deaf / late-deafened — definitions and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Prelingually deaf: born deaf or became deaf before learning language; postlingually deaf / late-deafened: lost hearing after learning to speak. Terms are acceptable but may need explanation for general audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurately and provide context when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: preferred pronouns — avoid phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the term 'preferred pronouns' because pronouns are not a preference but the appropriate way to refer to someone; use 'pronouns' instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'preferred pronouns' is acceptable only when someone uses more than one set and indicates a preference. Updated March 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pride Day — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Short for gay/lesbian pride; commonly used to indicate celebrations commemorating the Stonewall Inn riots (June 28, 1969), typically held in June.
